segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome back to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: My name is Katherine and today we have a very weather focused lesson.
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳，今天我们有一个非常注重天气的课程。

segments.en: It's all about all the horrible things that can happen to you with the weather.
segments.zh: 这都是关于天气可能发生在你身上的所有可怕的事情。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So as you know, there are many different types of weather and not only rain or sunshine but many other phenomena.
segments.zh: 如您所知，有许多不同类型的天气，不仅有雨或阳光，还有许多其他现象。

segments.en: So we're going to take a look at some of those but before we go into it, let's take a look at one word on Vocabulary Preview.
segments.zh: 所以我们要看看其中的一些，但在我们进入它之前，让我们看一下关于词汇预览的一个词。

segments.en: Vocabulary Preview.
segments.zh: 词汇预习。

segments.en: Okay, so we're talking about extreme weather today.
segments.zh: 好的，所以我们今天谈论的是极端天气。

segments.en: That's not rain or drizzle or sunshine.
segments.zh: 那不是下雨、毛毛雨或阳光。

segments.en: We're talking about really interesting, unique and sometimes devastating things that can happen.
segments.zh: 我们谈论的是真正有趣、独特、有时甚至是毁灭性的事情。

segments.en: So today's vocabulary word is Armageddon.
segments.zh: 所以今天的词汇是世界末日。

segments.en: Alright, so Armageddon.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以世界末日。

segments.en: Now you've probably seen the movie Armageddon.
segments.zh: 现在你可能已经看过电影世界末日了。

segments.en: So what does this word mean?
segments.zh: 那么这个词是什么意思呢？

segments.en: Okay, so this word is a reference to the end of the world.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以这个词是对世界末日的参考。

segments.en: It means the time when the world will end because of a great catastrophe or a great disaster.
segments.zh: 这意味着世界因一场大灾难或一场大灾难而结束的时代。

segments.en: Okay, so everyone talks about Armageddon.
segments.zh: 好的，所以每个人都在谈论世界末日。

segments.en: It's mentioned in the Bible and as you say, it's when the world stops existing.
segments.zh: 它在圣经中被提及，正如你所说，这是世界停止存在的时候。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So think about that one as we listen to today's dialogue.
segments.zh: 所以当我们听今天的对话时，想一想。

segments.en: We will be back in a minute to talk about what's going on.
segments.zh: 我们将在一分钟内回来讨论正在发生的事情。

segments.en: Those are the headlines for today and now for the International Weather Report with Mike Sanderson.
segments.zh: 以上是今天的头条新闻，接下来由迈克·桑德森带来国际天气预报。

segments.en: Thank you, Bob.
segments.zh: 谢谢你，鲍勃。

segments.en: This past week has been the beginning of Armageddon for many as a series of unprecedented meteorological events occurred around the world.
segments.zh: 过去的一周是世界各地发生的一系列前所未有的气象事件，对许多人来说是世界末日的开始。

segments.en: In Switzerland, a major avalanche was reported in the Alps.
segments.zh: 在瑞士，阿尔卑斯山报告了一场大雪崩。

segments.en: Fortunately, no one was injured.
segments.zh: 幸运的是，没有人受伤。

segments.en: Due to the extreme cold this winter, a blizzard has struck the U.S. Midwest, causing classes in schools and universities to be temporarily canceled.
segments.zh: 由于今年冬天的极端寒冷，一场暴风雪袭击了美国中西部，导致学校和大学的课程被暂时取消。

segments.en: Moving on to Latin America, Ecuador has suffered a six-month drought that has not only affected farming but has also forced the closure of the hydroelectric power plant that provides electricity for the entire country.
segments.zh: 再到拉丁美洲，厄瓜多尔遭受了为期六个月的干旱，这不仅影响了农业，而且迫使关闭为整个国家提供电力的水力发电厂。

segments.en: In Chile, a major earthquake that registered 7.5 on the Richter scale struck the southern region.
segments.zh: 在智利，里氏 7.5 级的大地震袭击了南部地区。

segments.en: Losses are reported to be in the billions.
segments.zh: 据报道，损失数十亿。

segments.en: Authorities have not yet released an official statement.
segments.zh: 当局尚未发表官方声明。

segments.en: Not a great week for the world.
segments.zh: 这一周对全世界来说都不太平。

segments.en: Any good news?
segments.zh: 有什么好消息吗？

segments.en: I'm afraid not, Bob.
segments.zh: 恐怕没有，鲍勃。

segments.en: One of the major volcanoes in Mexico has erupted, causing major floods and landslides in the region.
segments.zh: 墨西哥的主要火山之一已经喷发，导致该地区发生重大洪水和山体滑坡。

segments.en: Meanwhile, Mexico's coast has been hit by Hurricane Liliana and officials say that all the seismic activity leads them to believe that a tsunami may hit Central America, affecting Honduras, Guatemala, and Panama.
segments.zh: 与此同时，墨西哥海岸遭到飓风莉莲娜的袭击，官员们表示，所有地震活动都使他们相信海啸可能袭击中美洲，影响了洪都拉斯、危地马拉和巴拿马。

segments.en: That's all the news we have for today, but stay tuned for updates on the 6 o'clock news.
segments.zh: 这就是我们今天的所有新闻，但请继续关注 6 点新闻的更新。

segments.en: Back to you, Bob.
segments.zh: 接下来交还给你，鲍勃。

segments.en: All right, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: And well, this weather report is not really far from the truth.
segments.zh: 好吧，这份天气预报与事实相差不远。

segments.en: I mean, this kind of stuff happens every day all over the world, right?
segments.zh: 我的意思是，这种事情每天都在世界各地发生，对吧？

segments.en: That's correct.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And unfortunately, it's been happening very frequently in the past couple months.
segments.zh: 不幸的是，在过去的几个月里，这种情况经常发生。

segments.en: We've heard of a lot of earthquakes and volcanoes and things like that.
segments.zh: 我们听说过很多地震和火山之类的东西。

segments.en: So this is very valuable stuff when you're trying to talk about current events as well.
segments.zh: 因此，当您尝试谈论时事时，这也是非常有价值的东西。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So why don't we start now analyzing a couple of different words and phrases on Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 那么我们为什么不现在开始分析几个不同的单词和短语关于语言外卖。

segments.en: Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: Well, the first vocabulary item we have here is meteorological event.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们这里的第一个词汇项目是气象事件。

segments.en: It's a real mouthful.
segments.zh: 这是一个真正的嘴巴。

segments.en: It's a long word.
segments.zh: 这是一个很长的词。

segments.en: Meteorological.
segments.zh: 气象。

segments.en: So for example, meteorological means having to do with the weather, something that's related to the weather.
segments.zh: 例如，气象意味着与天气有关，这与天气有关。

segments.en: So a meteorological event could be rain, snow.
segments.zh: 所以气象事件可能是雨，雪。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So it has to do with meteorology.
segments.zh: 所以它与气象学有关。

segments.en: Meteorology is the study of the weather.
segments.zh: 气象学是对天气的研究。

segments.en: And someone who does this is a meteorologist.
segments.zh: 这样做的人是气象学家。

segments.en: So usually the weathermen that you see on TV, they're meteorologists.
segments.zh: 所以通常是你在电视上看到的气象员，他们是气象学家。

segments.en: So let's go now to Marco, our resident meteorologist.
segments.zh: 所以现在让我们去看看我们的常驻气象学家马可。

segments.en: There we go.
segments.zh: 好了。

segments.en: Our resident meteorologist.
segments.zh: 我们的常驻气象学家。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So meteorological events.
segments.zh: 所以气象事件。

segments.en: Now moving on, one of the first events that we're going to look at is an avalanche.
segments.zh: 现在继续前进，我们将要查看的首批事件之一是雪崩。

segments.en: Avalanche.
segments.zh: 雪崩。

segments.en: And avalanche has to do with snow.
segments.zh: 雪崩与雪有关。

segments.en: This means that when a mountain that has a lot of snow on it, maybe part of that snow breaks off and starts to roll down, you have a wall of snow that comes down.
segments.zh: 这意味着当一座山上有很多雪的山时，也许部分雪会折断并开始滚落，你就会有一堵雪墙掉下来。

segments.en: That's an avalanche.
segments.zh: 那是雪崩。

segments.en: That's an avalanche.
segments.zh: 那是雪崩。

segments.en: So you could say, avalanche.
segments.zh: 所以你可以说，雪崩。

segments.en: When the snow comes down.
segments.zh: 当雪落下时。

segments.en: And it's actually very dangerous because people can get buried under the snow.
segments.zh: 这实际上非常危险，因为人们可能会被雪埋在雪地下。

segments.en: Yeah, exactly.
segments.zh: 对，没错。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Another event that has to do with snow is a blizzard.
segments.zh: 另一个与雪有关的事件是暴风雪。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: A blizzard is different from an avalanche because an avalanche, maybe it's not snowing.
segments.zh: 暴风雪与雪崩不同，因为雪崩，也许没有下雪。

segments.en: The snow just falls.
segments.zh: 雪刚刚下落。

segments.en: But in a blizzard, you're talking about a storm of snow.
segments.zh: 但在暴风雪中，你说的是一场雪风暴。

segments.en: But it's like a lot of snow coming down from the sky.
segments.zh: 但这就像从天而降的大量雪。

segments.en: So much snow that you probably can't see anything.
segments.zh: 雪太多了，你可能看不到任何东西。

segments.en: There's just white everywhere.
segments.zh: 到处都是白色。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So that's a blizzard.
segments.zh: 所以这是一场暴风雪。

segments.en: A lot of, lot of snow coming down from the sky.
segments.zh: 很多，大量的雪从天而降。

segments.en: Now moving on, the opposite of snow and things being wet is we have a drought.
segments.zh: 现在继续前进，雪和潮湿的反面是我们有干旱。

segments.en: Yeah, this is the opposite of wet actually.
segments.zh: 是的，这实际上与湿的相反。

segments.en: So there's no rain in a drought.
segments.zh: 所以干旱中没有下雨。

segments.en: A drought means that things are very dry.
segments.zh: 干旱意味着事情非常干燥。

segments.en: The land is very dry.
segments.zh: 土地非常干燥。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So it's a period of time that there's no snow, there's no water, there's no rain, there's nothing.
segments.zh: 所以这是一段时间没有雪，没有水，没有下雨，什么都没有。

segments.en: It's very, very dry.
segments.zh: 它非常非常干燥。

segments.en: We're going through a drought.
segments.zh: 我们正在经历一场干旱。

segments.en: Correct.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: And the reason the problem with a drought is very dangerous is because people cannot grow food in a drought.
segments.zh: 干旱的问题非常危险的原因是人们无法在干旱中种植食物。

segments.en: And so lots of people starve when this happens.
segments.zh: 当这种情况发生时，很多人会挨饿。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So you got to watch out for a drought.
segments.zh: 所以你必须注意干旱。

segments.en: Now, in this case, it not only affected farming, but also we have a hydroelectric power plant that can't work, obviously, because there's no water.
segments.zh: 现在，在这种情况下，它不仅影响了农业，而且我们还有一个水力发电厂无法工作，显然，因为没有水。

segments.en: So hydro means water.
segments.zh: 所以水电是指水。

segments.en: Hydroelectric means electricity that is generated by flowing water.
segments.zh: 水电是指通过流动的水产生的电力。

segments.en: Well, a mill, something that turns water on a river is a way to get power from water.
segments.zh: 好吧，磨坊，在河流上流水的东西是从水中获取电力的一种方式。

segments.en: But a hydroelectric project that can give you electricity is maybe like a dam or an electric mill.
segments.zh: 但是一个可以给你电力的水电项目可能就像大坝或电厂一样。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So usually you have these on rivers and they just take advantage of the flowing of water to turn some huge turbines and generate power.
segments.zh: 所以通常你在河流上有这些，它们只是利用水的流动来转动一些巨大的涡轮机并发电。

segments.en: So that's all we have for now.
segments.zh: 所以这就是我们现在所拥有的一切。

segments.en: Why don't we listen to the dialogue again?
segments.zh: 我们为什么不再听对话？

segments.en: And we'll be back shortly to take a look at some more words.
segments.zh: 我们很快就会回来看看更多的单词。

segments.zh: 这些是今天的头条新闻。

segments.en: Well, a word that many people are unfortunately familiar with is Richter or Richter scale.
segments.zh: 好吧，不幸的是，许多人熟悉的词是里希特或里希特的规模。

segments.en: And now this is something that a lot of people are talking about right now because of the earthquake in Sichuan, China last year and the earthquake in Haiti very recently.
segments.zh: 而现在，由于去年四川的地震和海地的地震，很多人现在都在谈论这件事。

segments.en: And so the Richter scale, that's a big R because it's a proper name, is a way for us to determine how severe, how big the earthquake was.
segments.zh: 所以里氏尺度，这是一个很大的 R，因为它是一个专有名称，是我们确定地震有多严重、多大的一种方式。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So people talk about a 6.0, a 7.1.
segments.zh: 所以人们谈论一个 6.0，一个 7.1。

segments.en: So that's on the Richter scale.
segments.zh: 所以这是在里氏规模。

segments.en: The lowest is zero and the highest is 10, correct?
segments.zh: 最低为零，最高为 10，对吗？

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: But 10 is like impossible, apparently.
segments.zh: 但显然，10 是不可能的。

segments.en: Apparently.
segments.zh: 显然。

segments.en: And a lot of them are actually underwater, but the very serious ones are maybe 8.0, 7.0.
segments.zh: 其中很多实际上是在水下，但非常严重的可能是 8.0、7.0。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So Richter scale.
segments.zh: 所以里氏规模。

segments.en: Now we talked about earthquakes.
segments.zh: 现在我们谈到了地震。

segments.en: We talked about snowing.
segments.zh: 我们谈到了雪。

segments.en: Now let's talk about a volcano.
segments.zh: 现在让我们谈谈一座火山。

segments.en: A volcano in Mexico has erupted.
segments.zh: 墨西哥的一座火山爆发了。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So we've got two words here, volcano.
segments.zh: 所以我们在这里有两个词，火山。

segments.en: A volcano is a mountain that has an opening in the center where lava from the middle of the earth, the center of the earth, can come out.
segments.zh: 火山是一座山，在中心有一个开口的地方，从地球的中心，地球的中心可以出来的熔岩。

segments.en: So it's very dangerous, obviously, because it's very hot.
segments.zh: 所以这很危险，很明显，因为它很热。

segments.en: But a volcano doesn't open.
segments.zh: 但火山不开。

segments.en: It erupts.
segments.zh: 它爆发了。

segments.en: So the verb here that we use with a volcano is to erupt.
segments.zh: 所以我们在这里使用火山的动词是爆发。

segments.en: Okay, so it doesn't explode, a volcano erupts.
segments.zh: 好吧，它不会爆炸，火山爆发。

segments.en: That means to open violently, very quickly.
segments.zh: 这意味着非常快速地打开。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So when this happens, obviously you have a lot of lava, you have maybe snow that melts, and you have floods and landslides.
segments.zh: 所以当这种情况发生时，显然你有很多熔岩，你可能有雪融化，你有洪水和山体滑坡。

segments.en: Okay, landslides.
segments.zh: 好吧，滑坡。

segments.en: A landslide is one word, but it's made up of two words that you probably already know.
segments.zh: 滑坡是一个词，但它由您可能已经知道的两个词组成。

segments.en: So land, obviously it's the ground and things like that, the earth.
segments.zh: 所以土地，显然是地面和类似的东西，地球。

segments.en: But a slide is to move down across the ground.
segments.zh: 但是滑梯是在地面上向下移动。

segments.en: And so a landslide happens when you've got something like lava or water that's pushing all of the earth, all of the ground down.
segments.zh: 因此，当您有熔岩或水将整个地球推倒时，就会发生山体滑坡。

segments.en: And it's destroying houses and trees and land, and it's very, very destructive.
segments.zh: 它正在摧毁房屋、树木和土地，非常非常具有破坏性。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So you usually see this that happens on the side of mountains, on the side of hills, where all that land starts to slide down or to go down.
segments.zh: 所以你通常会看到这发生在山的一侧，山的一侧，所有的土地开始滑下或下降。

segments.en: And it's very similar to an avalanche, right?
segments.zh: 它与雪崩非常相似，对吧？

segments.en: But instead of snow falling down, it's land.
segments.zh: 但不是雪落下来，而是土地。

segments.en: Mud and land.
segments.zh: 泥土和土地。

segments.en: Mud, yeah.
segments.zh: 泥，是的。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So we have a landslide.
segments.zh: 所以我们有一个山体滑坡。

segments.en: And because of all the eruptions and the earthquakes, they said that they have a lot of seismic activity.
segments.zh: 由于所有的爆发和地震，他们说他们有很多地震活动。

segments.en: This word seismic is something that I've heard a lot recently in movies, like 2012.
segments.zh: 地震这个词是我最近在电影中听到的很多东西，比如 2012 年。

segments.en: So seismic means having to do with the movement of the plates under the earth's crust.
segments.zh: 所以地震意味着与地壳下的板块的运动有关。

segments.en: So the earth is not everything that we see.
segments.zh: 所以地球并不是我们所看到的一切。

segments.en: It's also activity, things happening underneath the ground.
segments.zh: 这也是活动，发生在地下的事情。

segments.en: And so underneath the ground, we have these big plates.
segments.zh: 所以在地下，我们有这些大盘子。

segments.en: And seismic activity is what happens when these kind of things start to move.
segments.zh: 地震活动是当这些事情开始移动时会发生什么。

segments.en: Activity is movement.
segments.zh: 活动是运动。

segments.en: And so seismic activity refers to earthquakes and volcanoes, things that are changing under the ground that will affect us.
segments.zh: 所以地震活动是指地震和火山，这些东西在地下发生了变化，会影响我们。

segments.en: OK.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So that's seismic activity.
segments.zh: 这就是地震活动。

segments.en: It's pronounced seismic, right?
segments.zh: 它的发音是地震，对吧？

segments.en: Seismic.
segments.zh: 地震。

segments.en: That's correct.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Seismic.
segments.zh: 地震。

segments.en: And because of all this activity, people say that they may have a tsunami.
segments.zh: 由于所有这些活动，人们说他们可能有海啸。

segments.en: Well, this doesn't sound very English, does it?
segments.zh: 嗯，这听起来不是很英语，不是吗？

segments.en: I know, tsunami.
segments.zh: 我知道，海啸。

segments.en: And actually, if you see the spelling, it's with a T, T-S.
segments.zh: 实际上，如果您看到拼写，它是带有 T、T-S 的。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: I think it's a Japanese word, but I'm not positive.
segments.zh: 我认为这是一个日语单词，但我并不积极。

segments.en: I think so, too.
segments.zh: 我也是这么想的。

segments.en: Tsunami is the name that we give to a giant tidal wave.
segments.zh: 海啸是我们给巨大潮汐的名字。

segments.en: So that's a wave of water in the ocean that's very, very dangerous because it can get to 100, 200 feet tall.
segments.zh: 所以这是海洋中的一波非常非常危险的水波，因为它可以达到 100、200 英尺高。

segments.en: And this means that when it comes down, it can destroy houses, cities, cars, things like that.
segments.zh: 这意味着当它倒下时，它可以摧毁房屋、城市、汽车之类的东西。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: And there was a very, very famous tsunami in Southeast Asia in 2004.
segments.zh: 2004年，东南亚发生了非常非常著名的海啸。

segments.en: Do you remember that?
segments.zh: 你还记得吗？

segments.en: Yeah, in Indonesia, right?
segments.zh: 是的，在印度尼西亚，对吧？

segments.en: That's right, in Indonesia and Thailand and Vietnam.
segments.zh: 没错，在印度尼西亚、泰国和越南。

segments.en: Yeah, it was intense.
segments.zh: 是的，很激烈。

segments.en: It was big.
segments.zh: 它很大。

segments.en: And it was also because of an earthquake, right?
segments.zh: 这也是因为地震，对吧？

segments.en: I think so.
segments.zh: 我想是的。

segments.en: All these earthquakes, they move the earth around.
segments.zh: 所有这些地震，它们都在移动地球。

segments.en: And then all of a sudden, the reaction is that there's water that moves.
segments.zh: 然后突然间，反应是有水在移动。

segments.en: And the water then turned into a wave.
segments.zh: 然后水变成了波浪。

segments.en: Yeah, just imagine what happens if you have a bucket of water and then you start moving the bucket just a little bit.
segments.zh: 是的，想象一下如果你有一桶水然后你开始稍微移动水桶会发生什么。

segments.en: You see how water starts to splat all over the place.
segments.zh: 你会看到水是如何开始溅到整个地方的。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: All right, so tsunami was our last word for today.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以海啸是我们今天的最后决定。

segments.en: Why don't we listen to our dialogue again and we'll be back shortly.
segments.zh: 我们为什么不再听我们的对话，我们很快就会回来。

segments.en: Those are the headlines for today.
segments.zh: 这些是今天的头条新闻。

segments.en: And now for the International Weather Report with Mike Sanderson.
segments.zh: 现在是与迈克·桑德森的国际天气报告。

segments.en: Thank you, Bob.
segments.zh: 谢谢你，鲍勃。

segments.en: This past week has been the beginning of Armageddon for many, as a series of unprecedented meteorological events occurred around the world.
segments.zh: 过去一周对许多人来说是世界末日的开始，因为世界各地发生了一系列前所未有的气象事件。

segments.en: In Switzerland, a major avalanche was reported in the Alps.
segments.zh: 在瑞士，阿尔卑斯山报告了一场大雪崩。

segments.en: Fortunately, no one was injured.
segments.zh: 幸运的是，没有人受伤。

segments.en: Due to the extreme cold this winter, a blizzard has struck the U.S. Midwest, causing classes in schools and universities to be temporarily canceled.
segments.zh: 由于今年冬天的极端寒冷，一场暴风雪袭击了美国中西部，导致学校和大学的课程被暂时取消。

segments.en: Moving on to Latin America, Ecuador has suffered a six-month drought that has not only affected farming but has also forced the closure of the hydroelectric power plant that provides electricity for the entire country.
segments.zh: 再到拉丁美洲，厄瓜多尔遭受了为期六个月的干旱，这不仅影响了农业，而且迫使关闭为整个国家提供电力的水力发电厂。

segments.en: In Chile, a major earthquake that registered 7.5 on the Richter scale struck the southern region.
segments.zh: 在智利，里氏 7.5 级的大地震袭击了南部地区。

segments.en: Losses are reported to be in the billions.
segments.zh: 据报道，损失数十亿。

segments.en: Authorities have not yet released an official statement.
segments.zh: 当局尚未发表官方声明。

segments.en: Not a great week for the world.
segments.zh: 这一周对全世界来说都不太平。

segments.en: Any good news?
segments.zh: 有什么好消息吗？

segments.en: I'm afraid not, Bob.
segments.zh: 恐怕没有，鲍勃。

segments.en: One of the major volcanoes in Mexico has erupted, causing major floods and landslides in the region.
segments.zh: 墨西哥的主要火山之一已经喷发，导致该地区发生重大洪水和山体滑坡。

segments.en: Meanwhile, Mexico's coast has been hit by Hurricane Liliana, and officials say that all the seismic activity leads them to believe that a tsunami may hit Central America, affecting Honduras, Guatemala and Panama.
segments.zh: 与此同时，墨西哥的海岸遭到飓风莉莲娜的袭击，官员们表示，所有地震活动都使他们相信海啸可能袭击中美洲，影响了洪都拉斯、危地马拉和巴拿马。

segments.en: That's all the news we have for today, but stay tuned for updates on The 6 O'Clock News.
segments.zh: 这就是我们今天的所有新闻，但请继续关注 6 点新闻的更新。

segments.en: Back to you, Bob.
segments.zh: 接下来交还给你，鲍勃。

segments.en: So Marco, these are all pretty terrifying.
segments.zh: 所以马可，这些都很可怕。

segments.en: Have you ever experienced a meteorological event like one of the ones that we talked about today?
segments.zh: 你有没有经历过像我们今天谈到的那样的气象事件？

segments.en: I've actually lived through like three earthquakes, like pretty big ones.
segments.zh: 我实际上经历了三场地震，就像相当大的地震一样。

segments.en: Plus, because you used to live in Los Angeles.
segments.zh: 另外，因为你以前住在洛杉矶。

segments.en: So you get them all the time in LA.
segments.zh: 所以你一直在洛杉矶得到它们。

segments.en: Apart from that, I actually, I've seen a volcano erupt a couple of times because, you know, Ecuador is a, is, is part of the volcano alley, right?
segments.zh: 除此之外，我实际上，我见过几次火山喷发，因为，你知道，厄瓜多尔是一个，是，是火山小巷的一部分，对吧？

segments.en: It's all the Andes mountains and it's part of the circle of fire, what they call.
segments.zh: 它是所有安第斯山脉，它是火圈的一部分，他们所说的。

segments.en: So we have a couple of different active volcanoes and from time to time they will start to smoke or to spew some lava, but nothing major.
segments.zh: 所以我们有几个不同的活火山，它们会不时开始冒烟或喷出一些熔岩，但没什么大不了的。

segments.en: Like there hasn't been a major catastrophe with the volcanoes.
segments.zh: 就像火山没有发生重大灾难一样。

segments.en: Hopefully it won't either.
segments.zh: 希望它也不会。

segments.en: Well, and these days they have a lot of equipment, seismic equipment and meteorological equipment that can help meteorologists to determine when things will happen, like when a volcano will erupt or if there will be an earthquake because they can study the tremors in the ground.
segments.zh: 好吧，这些天他们有很多设备、地震设备和气象设备，可以帮助气象学家确定什么时候会发生，比如火山何时爆发，或者是否会有地震，因为他们可以研究地面的地震。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: And I think probably the most famous volcano is, I think it was in Italy, right?
segments.zh: 我想可能最著名的火山是，我想是在意大利，对吧？

segments.en: Mount Vesuvius.
segments.zh: 维苏威火山。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And it was Mount Vesuvius in Naples, which famously destroyed a number of cities in this ancient civilization and ancient Roman times.
segments.zh: 那不勒斯的维苏威火山是著名的古代文明和古罗马时代的许多城市。

segments.en: It was.
segments.zh: 确实如此。

segments.en: And what's amazing is that they still have a lot of the, the buildings underground under the ash because when all the ash settled, it preserved the bodies like a mummy.
segments.zh: 令人惊讶的是，他们仍然有很多，在灰烬下的建筑物，因为当所有的灰烬都沉淀下来时，它就像木乃伊一样保存着尸体。

segments.en: And so you can see the bodies and the things that they, you know, their jewelry and their money.
segments.zh: 所以你可以看到他们，你知道的，他们的珠宝和他们的钱的身体和东西。

segments.en: And it's fascinating because it's this horrible, horrible natural disaster actually helped us in the future learn about this old civilization.
segments.zh: 它很吸引人，因为它是这种可怕的、可怕的自然灾害，实际上帮助我们将来了解这个古老的文明。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: It's crazy.
segments.zh: 太疯狂了。

segments.en: Actually in Ecuador you can see a huge hole that has like a lake in the middle and you're like, oh wow, that's beautiful.
segments.zh: 实际上，在厄瓜多尔，你可以看到一个巨大的洞，中间有一个湖，你会说，哦，哇，这很漂亮。

segments.en: But that's actually caused because the entire mountain just kind of blew the top off like the cone because of this major eruption.
segments.zh: 但这实际上是因为整个山峰只是因为这次大喷发而像锥体一样炸毁了顶部。

segments.en: So you can just imagine how powerful these eruptions are.
segments.zh: 所以你可以想象这些喷发有多强大。

segments.en: I can just imagine what it would have been like Mount Vesuvius.
segments.zh: 我可以想象它会像维苏威火山一样。

segments.en: But anyway, on a brighter note, if you have any questions, any comments or any stories of your own, maybe you've, you've lived through a typhoon, a hurricane or tornado, you can come to our website, EnglishPod.com.
segments.zh: 但无论如何，在一个更明亮的说明中，如果您有任何问题、任何评论或您自己的故事，也许您曾经经历过台风、飓风或龙卷风，您可以访问我们的网站 englishpod.com。

segments.en: We hope to see you there.
segments.zh: 希望到时候见到你。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Bye guys.
segments.zh: 大家再见。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。
